title: Bob Lyons and Perez, and playing loud
summary: A few jobs with Lyons, a Saturday job with Perez, and whether he was louder than other clarinetists.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. I want to ask you about Bob Lyons too. He had a band? Yeah, he had a band. You play with him much? Well, I played with him a little. Not long. But not with his group that he had when he hadn't been in. I don't know what had happened, but he just got a line up together. Little old boy he was playing, drum. I don't remember the other fellas than he had. But I didn't play but a few jobs with him. I see. And Baras, did you play many jobs with him? No, Baras? No, Baras. I only played a few times with him out at Bell & Boy. I didn't play with him but about, I guess about two, three times. Do you remember who was in the band? It wasn't his band. Oh, it was somebody else? No, it was Glass. Oh, yeah. And the Glass, you know, Booker T. It was Booker T's job. He just hired the men, you know. It was only four or five pieces. It was on Saturday night. We played out there about three or four times. Was Perez a get-off man or was he straight? He was straight and strong. Powerful. Powerful. But not raggy or would you say he was raggy? Not what raggy? Ratty. Ratty, you know. Would you call him a tongue? No, no. No, he wasn't a tongue. I got the picture of him and I don't know.

I notice now that- This was a good siren or trumpet. I notice now how most of the clarinet players around aren't as loud as you are. Back in the old days, would you say that you were louder than most of the clarinet players or were there a lot of them who can play as strong as you can?
I don't know. I don't think. I don't.
You think you were more as strong as them too, huh? Yeah.
